newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat slips on good crop forecasts, weather.
newsitem.headline: French wheat slips on good crop forecasts, weather.

text.p: New crop wheat slipped on Monday on improved harvest weather and prospects that France may produce another good crop this year, dealers said.
New crop wheat for September-December delivery was bid at 850 francs per tonne, down 10 francs on Friday, but there was no trade as sellers were still offering 860 francs.
"Buyers are bearish but there are no sellers," one dealer said.
Last week rain raised fears that new crop wheat quality could be hit and the harvest delayed, prompting millers and feed producers to turn to old crop for spot cover.
But dry conditions returned over the weekend, allowing farmers to start combining operations, and speculation over the size of the new harvest is now taking centre stage.
The latest crop forecasts suggest that while France may not repeat last year's record performance, it may still harvest a good crop, helped by higher sowings.
"We are not worried about quantity," one dealer said, adding that most operators were betting the harvest would reach "a good level".
According to industry sources, the national grain office ONIC expects a 1997 soft wheat yield of 6.9 tonnes per hectare against 7.3 tonnes last year, mostly the result of a prolonged spring drought.
Based on sowings of 4.95 million hectares estimated by ONIC on June 11, this would put the harvest at 34.2 million tonnes against a record 34.7 million in 1996.
The farm ministry is eyeing a soft wheat yield of 6.8 tonnes, which would put the crop at 33.3 million tonnes, industry sources said.
